ForgeCycle recursively merges JSON objects and replaces arrays wholesale. From
lowest to highest precedence, configuration comes from:

1. Built-in defaults
2. `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/forgecycle/config.json`
3. Checked-in `.forgecycle/config.json`
4. Ignored `.forgecycle/config.local.json`
5. Modeled command options such as `--policy`, `--base`, `--approval`,
   `--decomposer`, `--planner`, `--builder`, and `--reviewer`

Environment variables do not override ForgeCycle behavior. Provider credentials
are merely inherited by child CLIs and are never inspected by ForgeCycle.

The merged configuration is validated strictly: an unknown key, a value of the
wrong type, or a value outside its allowed set fails with exit 65, and the
error names the key, for example `invalid config: Configuration does not
match schema version 1: unknown field "retry"`. A value of the wrong type is
named by its full path, including candidate and policy names and array
indexes, for example `candidates.codex-high.timeout_seconds must be a number, not
string`. A key removed or renamed by an
upgrade fails the same way; rename or delete it. `forgecycle doctor` reports
the same error.

## Candidates and policies

Each candidate has a stable ID. A policy lists candidates for each of the four
roles: `decomposer` runs `roadmap decompose` and `roadmap
questions`, and `planner`, `builder`, and `reviewer` take the planning,
building, and reviewing turns of a task run. One candidate can serve several
roles, so name candidates by adapter and model rather than by role:

```json
{
  "candidates": {
    "codex-high": {
      "adapter": "codex",
      "model": "your-capable-model",
      "effort": "high",
      "permission": "unrestricted",
      "timeout_seconds": 0
    },
    "agy-low": {
      "adapter": "agy",
      "model": "your-fast-model",
      "effort": "low",
      "permission": "unrestricted"
    }
  },
  "policies": {
    "balanced": {
      "decomposer": ["codex-high"],
      "planner": ["codex-high"],
      "builder": ["agy-low"],
      "reviewer": ["codex-high"],
      "retry_sweeps": 2,
      "retry_backoff_seconds": 60
    }
  }
}
```

Effort is normalized to `low`, `medium`, or `high`. Permission is normalized to
`read-only`, `workspace-write`, or `unrestricted`; adapters map it to supported
native flags. Candidate arrays are ordered. ForgeCycle starts with the first
candidate and falls through deterministically when an invocation, provider, or
protocol error occurs. One malformed handoff receives one repair attempt. After
a full pass in which every candidate failed, candidates whose last failure was
retryable (a transient rate limit, timeout, or launch failure) get bounded retry
sweeps before the run blocks: `retry_sweeps` extra passes (default 2, maximum
10) after `retry_backoff_seconds` (default 60, maximum 3600). Protocol failures
are never retried — repair mode owns those.

The task loop reloads the merged configuration before every turn. Changes to
`.forgecycle/config.json`, the global config, or `config.local.json` take effect
on the next turn, including after `task resume` and automatic resume. One turn
uses one loaded configuration throughout. The task run keeps its selected policy
name; removing that policy or making the config invalid stops advancement with
exit 65 until the config is fixed. Explicit task approval settings stay in
force; otherwise the current defaults govern future turns. An approval already
awaiting a person remains pending.

`task run`, `task resume`, `roadmap run`, and `roadmap resume` accept `--planner
ID`, `--builder ID`, and `--reviewer ID`; `roadmap decompose` and `roadmap
questions` accept `--decomposer ID`. Each flag selects one candidate for that
role in the current invocation. The candidate must appear in that role's list
in the active policy. A candidate listed only for another role or policy is
rejected with exit 65. A read-only candidate cannot be `--builder`. To switch
a running task to a new candidate, first add it to the selected policy's list.

`forgecycle doctor` checks every policy's `decomposer`, `planner`, `builder`, and
`reviewer` lists: each must name known candidates without duplicates, use a
configured adapter, and (for `builder`) not be read-only. `forgecycle doctor
--ping` additionally invokes every candidate those lists reference, once each, in
read-only mode with its configured model and effort, and fails (exit 65) if any
does not answer; see [Recovery](/documentation/guides/recovery/#diagnose-setup).

Every policy must define all four lists, each non-empty; a configuration
without one is invalid. `forgecycle roadmap decompose` uses only the chosen
policy's `decomposer` candidates (it never falls back to `planner`) and forces
read-only permission for the assessment turn, regardless of the candidate's
configured permission. It validates the returned task graph before writing files.

When a provider exposes a useful level outside the normalized vocabulary, set
`native_effort` on that candidate. For example, Codex may support `xhigh` while an
OpenCode provider may use a named variant such as `max`. Every adapter passes it
in place of `effort`: Claude and agy as `--effort`, Codex as
`model_reasoning_effort`, and OpenCode as the `#variant` suffix of `--model`.
It is a single modeled override; ForgeCycle does not accept arbitrary native
arguments.

Arbitrary native argument strings are intentionally unsupported. The schema
models only flags ForgeCycle can validate without shell evaluation.

## Adapter configuration

```json
{
  "adapters": {
    "opencode": { "binary": "opencode" },
    "codex": { "binary": "codex" },
    "claude": { "binary": "claude" },
    "agy": { "binary": "agy", "print_timeout": "8760h" }
  }
}
```

Binary paths normally belong in `.forgecycle/config.local.json`. The `agy` print
timeout is intentionally large because that CLI defaults to five minutes and
does not document a disable value. ForgeCycle recognizes partial timeout output as
an adapter failure. Optional `timeout_seconds` is disabled when absent or zero.

To use Claude Code CLI, add a candidate with `"adapter": "claude"`, a Claude
model name or alias, and the desired permission level. Then put that candidate's
ID in the policy's `decomposer`, `planner`, `builder`, or `reviewer` lists. ForgeCycle checks
the `claude` binary only when a Claude candidate is configured.

## Quota cooldowns

```json
{ "quota_cooldown_seconds": 3600 }
```

When a candidate's provider reports an exhausted usage quota and names no
reset time, ForgeCycle skips that candidate for this many seconds (default
3600, maximum 604800). It records the cooldown in
`.forgecycle/adapter-cooldowns.json`, which `init` adds to `.gitignore`. A
reset time the provider does report always takes precedence.

## Worktree bootstrap

```json
{ "worktree": { "copy_ignored": ["local.properties"] } }
```

`git worktree add` checks out tracked files only, so ignored local
configuration that builds need (Android's `local.properties`, a `.env`) is
missing from each task worktree. Every `copy_ignored` entry must be a
repository-relative path with no `..`, must be ignored by Git, and must not be
tracked. `task run` and `doctor` check this with `git check-ignore` and `git
ls-files`, and reject violations with exit 65. `task run` copies each listed file
from the repository root into the new worktree, and `task resume` restores any that
are missing. Copies use mode `0600`. Missing sources are skipped. The copied
set is recorded as `provisioned_files` in `state.json` and named in each turn
manifest as `PROVISIONED_FILES`, so agents leave those files alone. `forgecycle
init` writes an empty list.

## Command lint rules

```json
{
  "lint": {
    "command_rules": [
      {
        "id": "agp-comma-class",
        "pattern": "class=[^ '\"]*,",
        "applies_to": ["plan", "review_added"],
        "message": "AGP runs only the first class of a comma list; loop per class"
      }
    ],
    "disabled_rules": []
  }
}
```

Use these rules to turn known project traps into validation errors instead of
documentation that agents forget. Each `pattern` is a Go RE2 regular
expression, compiled when the configuration loads. `applies_to` selects a
plan's `required_tests` (`plan`) and/or the tests a review adds beyond the
required set (`review_added`). A match is a repairable field error that quotes
`message`, so the same turn's repair call fixes it. The built-in rule
`no-tmp-scripts` rejects `/tmp` paths in review-added test commands. Disable it
by listing its ID in `disabled_rules`. Rule IDs must be unique, including
against built-ins.

## Review evidence reuse

```json
{ "review": { "evidence_reuse_paths": ["docs/**", "LEARNINGS.md", "README.md"] } }
```

Every review manifest names the files changed since the last review. When this
list is set and every changed path matches one of its globs (`**` spans
directories, `*` and `?` stay within one segment), the review may mark a
required test `reused: true`. It then carries over the previous review's passed
result instead of rerunning it. Leave the list unset to always
require independent reruns.

## Gates

```json
{
  "review": {
    "gates": [
      {
        "id": "app-connected",
        "command": "./gradlew :app:connectedDebugAndroidTest",
        "timeout_seconds": 5400,
        "cleanup": "adb -s emulator-5554 shell am force-stop com.example.app"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

A gate is a long-running required test that ForgeCycle runs itself before
each review instead of leaving it to an agent. Agents run commands
through their CLI's own tool, and those tools put time limits on commands, so
a suite that runs for an hour can be killed partway, and every retry starts
it again. A gate runs outside those limits, once per reviewed HEAD, and the
review reports its stored result.

- `id`: lowercase letters, digits, `-`, and `_`; unique.
- `command`: one line, run with `/bin/sh -c` from the worktree root. A plan
  gates a required test by copying this command verbatim; any other command,
  including a wrapped or abbreviated one, is an ordinary test.
- `timeout_seconds`: optional limit for one run; `0` or unset means none. A
  timeout fails the gate and stops its whole process group.
- `cleanup`: optional one-line command run after a timeout or an
  interruption (Ctrl-C or SIGTERM to ForgeCycle),
  for state the process group does not own. One example is instrumentation
  still running on a device after the Gradle client was stopped.

The gate's log, and a JSON result for a run that finished, are written under
`RUN_DIR/gates/<head>/`. Delete a result file to force the next review to
run that gate again. Gates must not change tracked or untracked files; write
reports to ignored build directories. A required test that checks those
reports is marked `after_gate: true` in the plan, and Reviewer runs it after
the gates. Agents read `GATES:`, `GATED_TESTS:`, and `AFTER_GATE_TESTS:` from
their manifests, and [the protocol](/documentation/reference/protocol/#gates) describes the
contract.

## Decomposition budget

```json
{ "decompose": { "max_acceptance_criteria": 6 } }
```

`forgecycle roadmap decompose` prints a warning for each generated task with more
acceptance criteria than this (default 6), recommending a split before running
it. Tasks are not rejected.

## Project guidance

The `instructions` array is an ordered list of repository-relative files every
role must inspect. Conventional defaults are `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and
`README.md`; missing files are ignored. Additional checked-in guidance can live
under `.forgecycle/instructions/`.

Each turn manifest lists only the files present in the run worktree, which
holds what is committed at the run base plus `worktree.copy_ignored` files. A
file that exists in your checkout but is uncommitted or Git-ignored never
reaches the agents. `task run` and `task resume` warn about such files on
stderr and record a `missing_instructions` diagnostic; `doctor` warns ahead of
time about files not committed at HEAD. Commit the file, or list an ignored
one in `worktree.copy_ignored`. The array replaces, rather than extends, the
list from a lower config layer.

## Approval configuration

`default_approval` selects the normal policy. `custom` reads checkpoints from the
task front matter first, then `approval.checkpoints` in config. Valid checkpoints
are `after_planning`, `after_building`, `after_reviewing`, and `final`; each
but `final` pauses after the phase it names, like the loop states.
The earlier names `after_plan`, `after_builder`, and `after_review` are
rejected with exit 65.

```yaml
---
forgecycle:
  approval: custom
  checkpoints: [after_planning, after_building, final]
  base: main
  change_expected: true
---
```

CLI options override task metadata. The input task is copied into the task
run directory at startup; later changes must arrive as human-feedback
artifacts.

### Approval in roadmap runs

A roadmap run pauses at its task runs' approval gates exactly as each task
run would on its own, so the approval policy decides how unattended it is.
`forgecycle roadmap run --approval POLICY` passes the policy to every task run
and overrides the tasks' front matter; without it, each task's front matter or
`default_approval` applies, and the roadmap run says when any task will pause:
`forgecycle: info: task runs will pause at approval gates (approval=<policy>)`.

| Approval | Pauses | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `autonomous` | never; only at stops | fully unattended roadmap runs |
| `custom` with `approval.checkpoints: ["final"]` (`roadmap run --approval custom`) | once per task, before the task run finishes | reviewing each task before the next one starts |
| `plan-and-final` | twice per task | reviewing plans as well as results |

To review each task before the next one starts, set the checkpoint in
`.forgecycle/config.json`:

```json
{
  "approval": { "checkpoints": ["final"] }
}
```

and start the roadmap run with `--approval custom`. In an attached terminal
each child task run asks for approval inline and the roadmap run continues by
itself. Detached, a gate stops the roadmap run with exit 21: run
`forgecycle task approve <task-run-id>`, which finishes the task run and
prints the `roadmap resume` line, then `forgecycle roadmap resume
<roadmap-run-id>`. A roadmap task must not set `forgecycle.base`; the roadmap
run chooses every base, and its preflight rejects such a task with exit 65.

There is no budget guard. Spend is bounded by the approval policy, the
progress rule of `--auto-resume`, the no-progress check (three reviews with
unchanged findings), and the roadmap run stopping at the first stop that
remains.
